summary: Summation No. 17 covers South Korea under USAMGIK for February 1947. The central political event is the nomination (6 Feb) and swearing-in (10 Feb) of Ahn Chai Hong as the first Korean Civil Administrator, part of Hodge's policy of transferring administration to Koreans. The Interim Legislative Assembly dealt with the Antitrusteeship Resolution, and the Chief U.S. Commissioner issued four statements on the Moscow Decision and trusteeship, followed by Hodge's 15 February appeal to end agitation. Student strikes closed Seoul National University classes taught by Americans. Economic sections report 1947 crop goals, coal and paper shortages, a first fall in Bank of Chosen notes, new international postal service, rice collection at 83 percent of quota, and the new Services of Civilian Supply. Social sections cover refugee feeding, typhus and typhoid, Red Cross reorganization and press comment. The charts and tables give historians quantitative series.
highlights: On 6 February the Military Governor nominated Ahn Chai Hong as first Korean Civil Administrator; the Legislative Assembly confirmed him and he took the oath on 10 February 1947 after resigning his Assembly seat.

The Chief U.S. Commissioner issued four statements on the Moscow Decision (Joint Commission functions, procedure, Provisional Government, trusteeship), and Hodge on 15 February urged Koreans to end antitrusteeship agitation delaying independence.

The Legislative Assembly defeated, 49 to none with 10 abstentions, a proposal to use Japanese technicians in industry; the Military Governor's letters listed 11 matters for action, including a franchise law and land reform.

On 14 February the Military Governor withdrew American instructors from Seoul National University after student strikes; middle-school students in Seoul, Inchon, Suwon and Kunsan struck in sympathy from 10 February.
Bank of Chosen notes outstanding fell by 588,417,315 yen to 17,689,196,182.90 yen on 28 February, the first reversal of the rise begun in 1945; 83 percent of the rice quota had been collected.
The Services of Civilian Supply replaced the Office of the Coordinator of Civilian Supply to plan and handle all civilian supply imports into Korea.
Typhus rose from 147 to 271 cases and typhoid reached 659, mostly in Kyongsang-pukto; 256 people were bitten in the Cheju-do rabies outbreak, with 17 deaths.
The Korean Coast Guard Academy opened at Chinhae on 7 February and the cutter Admiral Lee, the first steel ship built in Korea since liberation, was christened.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Library covers, title page for Number 17 (February 1947), table of contents, and a list of 37 charts plus a map of Korea.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Overview: Ahn Chai Hong named Civil Administrator, Services of Civilian Supply created, 533,929 tons of rice collected, student strikes and refugee feeding.

sections.title: Section 1. Political Activities
sections.summary: Ahn Chai Hong sworn in 10 February; Assembly worked on the Antitrusteeship Resolution; Joint Commission reports issued; public order calm; Coast Guard Academy opened 7 February.

sections.title: Section 2. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Nine-crop 1947 estimate of 133,365,911 bushels; coal and cement stoppages; Bank of Chosen notes at 17.69 billion yen; new international mail; 533,929 tons of rice collected.

sections.title: Section 3. Social Activities
sections.summary: Refugee feeding at Pusan and Chinhae, Red Cross reorganization, typhus rise to 271, Seoul University strikes, and press focus on antitrusteeship.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Government and politics (Civil Administrator, Assembly, Joint Commission statements, Chinese representative Liu Yu-wen) and public safety (police chiefs' conference, prisons, Coast Guard, Constabulary).

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Ahn Chai Hong's appointment and statement, Assembly business, four Joint Commission reports on the Moscow Decision, Hodge's 15 February statement, and arrival of Chinese representative Liu Yu-wen.

sections.title: Administration
sections.summary: Ahn Chai Hong nominated 6 February and sworn in 10 February; his policy statement; new census in Kyonggi-do and Seoul; Services of Civilian Supply created.

sections.title: Korean Interim Legislative Assembly
sections.summary: Antitrusteeship Resolution; 49-0 defeat of the Japanese-technicians proposal; Military Governor's letters on rice rumors, Seoul National University and 11 pending matters; budget and Red Cross.

sections.title: U. S.-U. S. S. R. Joint Commission
sections.summary: Hodge's 5 February statement, four Chief Commissioner reports on Moscow Decision phases, Provisional Government and trusteeship, then Hodge's 15 February appeal against disorder.

sections.title: Foreign Affairs
sections.summary: Liu Yu-wen, official Chinese Government representative, arrived in Seoul on 5 February and took up quarters in the former Chinese Legation.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety
sections.summary: No disorders in February; first police chiefs' conference 7-8 February; 7,505 crimes in December; Taegu and Pusan prison camps; Coast Guard Academy, cutter Admiral Lee and Pohang base.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Natural resources, industry, commerce, and rationing and price control, with charts on production, finance, trade, mail, food stocks and prices.

sections.title: Section 1. Natural Resources
sections.summary: 1947 target of 86.6 million bushels of paddy rice; December fish landings of 33,609 tons; January coal output of 17,000 tons; tungsten 424 tons in 1946.

sections.title: Section 2. Industry
sections.summary: Raw-material shortages closed the Inchon fertilizer plant and beer breweries; paper output 433,105 pounds; sericulture conference; 775 operating factories with 43,868 workers; wage indexes.

sections.title: Section 3. Commerce
sections.summary: Currency fell 588 million yen; Monopoly Bureau; 122 property allocations; Hongkong liaison office; electricity use of 30.9 million kWh; new international mail rates and postal data.

sections.title: Section 4. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Services of Civilian Supply replaced the Coordinator's office; 83 percent of rice quota collected; food allocations, coal and petroleum, metal prices; 2,771 price violations.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health and welfare, education, culture and religion, and public information, ending with a map of Korea and blank scan pages.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Refugee rations for 12,475 at Pusan; Red Cross plan with 60 incorporators; 356 Japanese repatriated; nursing schools with 610 students; typhus 271, typhoid 659; cholera program for 1 April.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Culture and Religion
sections.summary: American instructors removed from Seoul National University 14 February; new Board of Regents plan; middle-school strikes; Language Purification Committee; 20,808 Youth Movement members.

sections.title: Section 3. Public Information
sections.summary: Rice-collection publicity, new Assembly radio program, Military Governor's 21 February rebuke of Dok Lib Sin Bo, press comment on antitrusteeship groups and school strikes; map of Korea.
